questions.stem: What does Security & Access Control Modelling define?
options: How data is physically partitioned across disks
Structured rules for who can access what data, under which conditions and in what manner
The semantic meaning of business concepts
The schedule for refreshing a data warehouse
The calculation logic of machine learning features
questions.explanation: Security & Access Control Modelling formalises data protection through roles, permissions, entitlements and policies that determine who can access what, under which conditions and how.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the core entities defined in Security & Access Control Modelling?
options: Users
Roles
Permissions
Policies
Dimensions
questions.explanation: The core entities are Users, Roles, Permissions and Policies; dimensions belong to dimensional modelling, not access control.

questions.stem: In a typical access control model, how are users, roles and permissions connected?
options: Permissions are assigned directly to users, and roles are decorative labels
Roles are assigned to permissions, and users inherit nothing
Users are assigned to roles, and roles carry permissions
Users and roles are the same entity
Policies replace both roles and permissions
questions.explanation: Typically users are assigned to roles, roles carry permissions, and policies add constraints such as time, location or device.

options: Restricts access to specific rows based on attributes such as branch assignment
Masks or hides sensitive columns such as Salary
Encrypts the entire table at rest
Limits the number of rows a query may return
Prevents users from creating new tables
questions.explanation: Row-Level Security restricts access to particular rows based on attributes, for example allowing a Branch Officer to see only loans in their own branch.

questions.stem: Which control masks or hides sensitive fields such as LoanAmount?
options: Row-Level Security
Attribute-Based Access Control
Policy-based time restrictions
Column-Level Security
Role explosion
questions.explanation: Column-Level Security (CLS) masks or hides sensitive fields such as Salary or LoanAmount.

questions.stem: What does Attribute-Based Access Control (ABAC) base its rules on?
options: Only the user's job title
Only the table's primary key
The database vendor's default settings
The order in which users were created
User attributes, data attributes and environmental conditions
questions.explanation: ABAC enforces rules based on a combination of user attributes, data attributes and environmental conditions.

questions.stem: In the loan approval example from I Am Datapedia!, what condition applies to Risk Managers' full access?
options: Only for loans in their own branch
Only during office hours and from corporate-managed devices
Only for loans below a certain amount
Only after approval by a Branch Officer
Only through the BI dashboard
questions.explanation: Risk Managers have full access but only during office hours and from corporate-managed devices, an example of policy-based access control.

options: A security breach caused by a compromised administrator role
The automatic deletion of unused roles
A situation where too many narrowly defined roles become difficult to manage
The merging of all roles into a single super-user role
A performance failure when a role has too many users
questions.explanation: Role explosion occurs in large organisations when too many narrowly defined roles are created and become hard to manage.

options: Slow query performance caused by security checks
The gradual expansion of a data warehouse
Users losing permissions after a role change
Users accumulating permissions over time without disciplined governance
Unauthorised access by external hackers
questions.explanation: Access creep happens when, without disciplined governance and change management, users accumulate permissions over time.

questions.stem: Which regulations are named as examples that a well-designed security model helps comply with?
options: GDPR and PCI DSS
SOX and Basel III
HIPAA and FERPA
ISO 9001 and ISO 14001
COBIT and ITIL
questions.explanation: The loan approval example states that such a model ensures compliance with regulations such as GDPR or PCI DSS.
